story: Assess the active solution before changing project targets
title: Inventory active framework, package and configuration dependencies
implementationInstructions: Run solution-scoped scans against only the projects listed in WARP_Prototype.Master.sln. Identify target frameworks, project formats, framework-only APIs, package references, configuration access, ServiceBuilder usage, Factories references and legacy hosting dependencies. Legacy ExpressUI and legacy WorkflowManager.API remain in the solution for this assessment so they can be inventoried and used as the behaviour-comparison baseline.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The inventory is generated from the active solution project list rather than the whole repository.
2. Every active project has entries for target framework, project format, package compatibility, hosting model and configuration model.
3. Framework-specific APIs and unsupported packages are mapped to follow-up backlog tasks.
4. Projects outside WARP_Prototype.Master.sln are excluded unless explicitly brought into scope.

story: Assess the active solution before changing project targets
title: Scan active projects for target frameworks and project format
implementationInstructions: For each active C# project, record whether it is legacy non-SDK or SDK-style, its current target framework declaration, custom imports, assembly-info generation, content/resource handling and any conditional property groups.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Every active C# project is classified as legacy or SDK-style.
2. Current target framework declarations are recorded.
3. Custom imports, generated AssemblyInfo behaviour and resource/content handling are identified.
4. The results identify which projects require SDK-style conversion before multi-targeting.

story: Assess the active solution before changing project targets
title: Scan active projects for framework-specific code and legacy dependencies
implementationInstructions: Search active projects for System.Web, OWIN/Katana, SignalR, Topshelf, ConfigurationManager, App.config/Web.config, Castle Windsor, ServiceBuilder, Factories.csproj, EPPlus, ExcelLibrary and other .NET Framework-specific APIs.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Each hit identifies the active project, source file and usage type.
2. Package references are distinguished from executable code usage.
3. Each confirmed active dependency is assigned a migrate, replace, remove or defer action.
4. No action is created for dependencies found only outside the active solution.

epic: Solution scope and safe project rationalisation
story: Define the migration solution boundary and remove only non-behavioural projects
title: Establish the active migration solution (safe removals only)
implementationInstructions: Use Solutions\WARP_Prototype.Master.sln as the authoritative migration scope. At this stage remove ONLY projects that carry no behavioural baseline value: stress-test projects, obsolete test utilities, and worker host shells already fully replaced by the .NET 10 daemon projects. Do NOT remove the legacy ExpressUI or legacy WorkflowManager.API hosts here. Those remain in the solution as the behavioural reference and as the discovery/inventory and behaviour-comparison target until their ASP.NET Core replacements are functionally complete and signed off; their removal is deferred to STORY-016.
acceptanceCriteria: 1. Only projects with no behavioural baseline value (stress-test, obsolete test utilities, already-replaced host shells) are removed from the active solution. 2. Legacy ExpressUI and legacy WorkflowManager.API remain in the solution and are explicitly retained for discovery, endpoint inventory and behaviour comparison (decommissioned later under STORY-016). 3. The solution loads without missing-project warnings. 4. A clean solution build succeeds.

epic: Solution scope and safe project rationalisation
story: Define the migration solution boundary and remove only non-behavioural projects
title: Remove obsolete worker host projects
implementationInstructions: Remove the legacy *Host projects that are replaced by the .NET 10 daemon projects, including ExpressManagerHost, FileCopierHost, FileDeleterHost, HydraJobManagerHost and RatCatManagerHost.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Obsolete host projects are absent from the solution.
2. Equivalent daemon projects remain present where required.
3. No active project references the removed hosts.
4. Build and deployment documentation no longer relies on the removed projects.

epic: Solution scope and safe project rationalisation
story: Define the migration solution boundary and remove only non-behavioural projects
title: Remove non-production stress and legacy test projects
implementationInstructions: Remove stress-test projects, TestConsole and legacy UnitTests from the active solution. Record replacement testing needs separately rather than carrying incompatible projects into the runtime migration.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The projects are absent from the active solution.
2. Their removal does not remove runtime code required by production projects.
3. The solution builds successfully.
4. Required replacement tests are captured in the validation epic.

story: Introduce a controlled net48/net10.0 compatibility phase
title: Enable active projects to build for both .NET Framework 4.8 and .NET 10
implementationInstructions: Temporarily multi-target eligible active projects to net48 and net10.0 so compatibility issues can be identified and resolved incrementally before removing the .NET Framework target. Preserve the existing net48 runtime behaviour while adding a net10.0 build path.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Each eligible active project declares both net48 and net10.0 in TargetFrameworks.
2. Projects that cannot be multi-targeted are identified and handled through an explicit replacement or host-migration task.
3. Target-specific references and source branches are limited to genuine framework incompatibilities and are clearly documented in the project file or code.
4. The net48 build continues to succeed without behavioural regression.
5. The net10.0 build succeeds for the multi-targeted project set.

story: Introduce a controlled net48/net10.0 compatibility phase
title: Assess projects for temporary multi-targeting
implementationInstructions: Review every project retained in WARP_Prototype.Master.sln and classify it as: suitable for net48/net10.0 multi-targeting, requires a replacement .NET 10 host/project, or should be removed from the migration solution. Record framework-specific package, API and hosting constraints.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Every active project has a documented classification.
2. The assessment identifies System.Web, Windows Service hosting, App.config, package compatibility and unsupported API constraints.
3. Projects requiring replacement hosts are linked to separate backlog tasks rather than forced into multi-targeting.
4. The proposed target-framework approach is agreed before project files are changed.

story: Introduce a controlled net48/net10.0 compatibility phase
title: Convert eligible legacy projects to SDK-style format
implementationInstructions: Convert eligible non-SDK project files to SDK-style while preserving source inclusion, embedded resources, content files, assembly metadata, project references and build output. Keep business logic unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Eligible projects use the SDK-style project format.
2. Legacy imports and explicit Compile items are removed only where SDK defaults provide equivalent behaviour.
3. Duplicate AssemblyInfo generation is resolved explicitly.
4. Embedded resources, content files and copy-to-output behaviour remain correct.
5. The existing net48 build still succeeds before net10.0 is added.

story: Introduce a controlled net48/net10.0 compatibility phase
title: Assess and remediate package compatibility for net10.0
implementationInstructions: Review every direct package reference in active projects. Upgrade, replace or remove packages that do not support net10.0, while avoiding unnecessary library changes where the existing package remains compatible.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Every active direct package has a documented compatibility outcome.
2. Unsupported packages have a replacement or removal task.
3. Reference-only packages are removed.
4. Licensing implications are reviewed for packages such as Excel libraries where relevant.
5. Restore succeeds for both target frameworks after changes.

story: Introduce a controlled net48/net10.0 compatibility phase
title: Add net10.0 alongside net48 in eligible projects
implementationInstructions: Update eligible project files to use `<TargetFrameworks>net48;net10.0</TargetFrameworks>`. Add the minimum conditional package references, framework references and compile conditions required to make both targets build. Do not redesign business logic during this step.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Eligible projects target both net48 and net10.0.
2. Target-specific package and framework references are scoped with explicit conditions.
3. Shared business code remains common between targets wherever possible.
4. Both target builds complete successfully for each converted project.
5. Any remaining incompatibility is captured as a separate migration task with a clear owner and acceptance criteria.

story: Introduce a controlled net48/net10.0 compatibility phase
title: Preserve SQL projects during the .NET migration
implementationInstructions: Retain SQL projects in the solution without attempting to assign them a .NET target framework. Verify that database project loading and build behaviour are unaffected by C# project changes.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. SQL projects remain present and load successfully.
2. No .NET TargetFramework property is added to SQL projects.
3. Database scripts, schemas and deployment artefacts remain unchanged unless explicitly required.
4. The complete solution build process handles SQL projects as expected.

story: Convert active projects to a single supported target framework
title: Consolidate active projects on net10.0
implementationInstructions: After the temporary dual-target phase has exposed and resolved compatibility issues, remove net48 from retained projects and eliminate framework-specific compile branches that are no longer required.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Every active C# project targets net10.0 only.
2. No active project contains net48 in TargetFramework or TargetFrameworks.
3. No active source file contains a required `#if NET48` path.
4. A clean restore and solution build succeed.

story: Convert active projects to a single supported target framework
title: Replace multi-targeting with net10.0
implementationInstructions: Update each retained SDK-style project from net48/net10.0 multi-targeting to a single `<TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>` declaration.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Active project files contain only net10.0 as the target framework.
2. Conditional package or reference groups that only applied to net48 are removed or made unconditional where still needed.
3. Restore completes without target-framework compatibility errors.
4. The complete solution builds.

story: Convert active projects to a single supported target framework
title: Remove NET48 conditional code
implementationInstructions: Review and remove `#if NET48`, `#else` and `#endif` branches that are no longer needed after the solution becomes net10.0-only. Preserve the .NET 10 behaviour path.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. No active code path depends on the NET48 compilation constant.
2. Removed branches do not change the intended .NET 10 behaviour.
3. The solution compiles without preprocessor-related errors.
4. Smoke tests pass for the affected components.

story: Create the .NET 10 application hosts that replace legacy web and service projects
title: Establish replacement ASP.NET Core and daemon projects
implementationInstructions: Create or confirm the .NET 10 replacement projects for ExpressUI.Core, WorkflowManager.API.Core and the daemon hosts. Keep responsibilities equivalent to the legacy hosts and avoid broad architecture redesign.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. ExpressUI.Core and WorkflowManager.API.Core exist as buildable net10.0 projects.
2. Required daemon replacement projects exist and target net10.0.
3. Each replacement project has the project references and configuration required for its current responsibility.
4. Legacy host removal does not leave an unowned runtime responsibility.

story: Create the .NET 10 application hosts that replace legacy web and service projects
title: Create or validate ExpressUI.Core host
implementationInstructions: Configure ExpressUI.Core as the replacement ASP.NET Core application for the required UI-facing API/controller functionality.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The project targets net10.0 and starts through Program.cs.
2. Controllers and routing are enabled.
3. Required shared projects and direct packages are referenced explicitly.
4. The application starts with representative configuration.

story: Create the .NET 10 application hosts that replace legacy web and service projects
title: Create or validate WorkflowManager.API.Core host
implementationInstructions: Configure WorkflowManager.API.Core as the replacement ASP.NET Core API host for selected WorkflowManager endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The project targets net10.0 and starts through Program.cs.
2. Controllers, routing, JSON options and DI are configured.
3. Required domain and data-access projects are referenced.
4. The API starts and responds to a basic health or test endpoint.

story: Create the .NET 10 application hosts that replace legacy web and service projects
title: Create or validate .NET 10 daemon host projects
implementationInstructions: Ensure ExpressManagerDaemon, HydraJobManagerDaemon, FileCopierDaemon and RatCatManagerDaemon are net10.0 executable projects with equivalent runtime responsibilities to the legacy service hosts.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Each required daemon is present in the active solution.
2. Each daemon targets net10.0 and has an executable Program.cs.
3. Required worker and service references are present.
4. Each daemon can be built independently.

story: Replace legacy ASP.NET and OWIN startup infrastructure
title: Move web application startup to ASP.NET Core
implementationInstructions: Replace Global.asax, System.Web startup and OWIN/Katana bootstrapping with ASP.NET Core Program.cs configuration. Preserve only the hosting, routing, authentication, logging and error-handling behaviour required by active functionality.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Active web hosts use Program.cs and the ASP.NET Core middleware pipeline.
2. Controller routing and JSON behaviour are configured explicitly.
3. Logging and exception handling are available at startup and request time.
4. No active host depends on Global.asax, System.Web or OWIN startup.

story: Replace legacy ASP.NET and OWIN startup infrastructure
title: Configure ASP.NET Core routing, JSON, logging and exception handling
implementationInstructions: Add the minimum middleware and service registrations required for controller discovery, endpoint routing, JSON serialisation, structured logging and consistent exception responses.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Controllers are discovered and mapped.
2. Request/response JSON remains compatible with active clients.
3. Unhandled exceptions are logged and converted to controlled responses.
4. Startup and request logs contain enough context for diagnosis.

story: Replace legacy ASP.NET and OWIN startup infrastructure
title: Assess and migrate required authentication and authorisation
implementationInstructions: Identify which legacy authentication flows are actually required by active endpoints. Implement only the required ASP.NET Core equivalent and do not carry forward unused social providers or unused OWIN packages.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Required authentication mechanisms are explicitly identified.
2. Required endpoints enforce equivalent authorisation rules.
3. Unused cookie, OAuth or third-party provider integrations are not migrated.
4. Authenticated and unauthorised request scenarios are tested.

story: Restore required business endpoints in ExpressUI.Core
title: Migrate missing ExpressUI functionality to ASP.NET Core
implementationInstructions: Recreate the required controllers, models, repository contracts and repository implementations in ExpressUI.Core without redesigning the business flow.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Required endpoints exist in ExpressUI.Core with the expected routes and HTTP verbs.
2. Request and response contracts match the legacy behaviour required by the current UI/client.
3. Repository dependencies are resolved through DI.
4. End-to-end business flow completes successfully.

story: Restore required business endpoints in ExpressUI.Core
title: Implement LoadImportSelectionData endpoint
implementationInstructions: Add or correct the controller action responsible for loading import selection data, including the expected route, POST binding and repository call.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The endpoint accepts the expected POST request and no longer returns HTTP 405.
2. Input validation matches the legacy behaviour required by callers.
3. Successful requests return the expected payload shape.
4. Repository failures are handled through the existing error-handling approach.

story: Restore required business endpoints in ExpressUI.Core
title: Implement DLM selections import repository
implementationInstructions: Create the concrete repository that implements IDlmSelectionsImportRepository and move the required database calls into the active .NET 10 data-access path.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. A concrete repository implements every interface member.
2. SQL, stored procedure names and parameter mapping preserve legacy behaviour.
3. The repository is registered in DI and can be resolved by the controller.
4. Integration or smoke testing confirms data is returned correctly.

story: Restore required business endpoints in ExpressUI.Core
title: Implement LoadDlmSubmissionData endpoint
implementationInstructions: Migrate the controller, request/response models and repository interactions needed to load DLM submission data.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The endpoint is available under the expected route and HTTP verb.
2. Returned data matches the shape required by the consuming UI/client.
3. Invalid or missing input produces a controlled response.
4. The endpoint succeeds against representative data.

story: Restore required business endpoints in ExpressUI.Core
title: Implement SubmitDlmProfiles endpoint
implementationInstructions: Migrate the DLM profile submission controller and its supporting repository/service calls into ExpressUI.Core.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Valid submissions are accepted and processed successfully.
2. Validation errors return the expected status and message format.
3. The database operation preserves the existing transaction and error behaviour.
4. A full load-and-submit workflow completes successfully.

story: Inventory and prioritise legacy WorkflowManager endpoints
title: Create an endpoint inventory and select a pilot vertical slice
implementationInstructions: Inventory legacy WorkflowManager.API endpoints, classify each as migrate, retire or defer, and select a low-risk pilot endpoint to establish the repeatable migration pattern.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Every legacy endpoint is listed with route, verb, controller/action and key dependencies.
2. Each endpoint is classified as migrate, retire or defer.
3. A pilot endpoint is selected with clear rationale.
4. The pilot includes controller, service/domain, data access, configuration and validation concerns.

story: Inventory and prioritise legacy WorkflowManager endpoints
title: Build the WorkflowManager endpoint inventory
implementationInstructions: Extract endpoint information from the legacy API project and capture route, HTTP verb, request model, response model, authentication requirement, domain dependencies and database dependencies.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The inventory covers every controller action in the legacy API project.
2. Duplicate or obsolete endpoints are identified.
3. Dependencies are recorded at sufficient detail to estimate migration effort.
4. The inventory is stored as a project artefact that can be reviewed by the team.

story: Inventory and prioritise legacy WorkflowManager endpoints
title: Implement and validate a pilot WorkflowManager endpoint
implementationInstructions: Migrate one selected endpoint end-to-end into WorkflowManager.API.Core, including route, request/response contracts, DI, domain calls, data access and tests. Use the result as the migration template for remaining endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The pilot endpoint is callable in WorkflowManager.API.Core.
2. Its request and response behaviour matches the legacy endpoint for representative inputs.
3. Required dependencies are resolved through DI.
4. Database behaviour is equivalent.
5. Lessons from the pilot are reflected in subsequent endpoint tasks.

story: Make active projects declare their own direct dependencies
title: Remove accidental dependency leakage through Factories
implementationInstructions: Remove project references that exist only to make transitive packages available. Add direct package or project references to the projects that actually use those APIs.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Active projects compile without relying on Factories for unrelated transitive dependencies.
2. Direct dependencies are declared in the consuming project.
3. No runtime behaviour changes are introduced.
4. The solution builds and affected workflows pass smoke testing.

story: Make active projects declare their own direct dependencies
title: Remove Factories reference from ExpressUI.Core
implementationInstructions: Remove the ExpressUI.Core project reference to Factories after identifying and replacing any transitive dependency that the project was consuming.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. ExpressUI.Core.csproj no longer references Factories.csproj.
2. The project has direct references for every API it uses.
3. All repository classes compile.
4. ExpressUI.Core starts and the migrated endpoints pass smoke testing.

story: Make active projects declare their own direct dependencies
title: Add direct Dapper dependency to ExpressUI.Core
implementationInstructions: Add Dapper directly to ExpressUI.Core because the repository layer uses Query, Execute, DynamicParameters and table-valued parameter extensions.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. ExpressUI.Core declares a direct Dapper package reference.
2. Repository extension methods compile without Factories.
3. The package version is compatible with net10.0.
4. Data-access smoke tests succeed.

story: Move active runtime configuration to the .NET configuration model
title: Replace App.config and ConfigurationManager usage
implementationInstructions: Use appsettings.json, environment variables and Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration for active .NET 10 hosts. Preserve existing setting names and defaults where practical.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Active hosts start without reading App.config or Web.config.
2. Required settings can be supplied through appsettings.json and environment variables.
3. Missing mandatory settings fail with a clear startup error.
4. Environment overrides work without code changes.

story: Move active runtime configuration to the .NET configuration model
title: Inventory legacy configuration usage
implementationInstructions: Scan the active solution for ConfigurationManager.AppSettings, ConnectionStrings, ApplicationSettingsBase, App.config, Web.config and generated Settings classes.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Every active legacy configuration read is listed with project, file and setting name.
2. Each item is classified as migrate, remove or retain temporarily.
3. Inactive files outside the solution are excluded from the migration backlog.
4. Follow-up tasks exist for each active runtime dependency.

story: Move active runtime configuration to the .NET configuration model
title: Configure daemon WarpUrl and logging through appsettings.json
implementationInstructions: Add appsettings.json configuration for Daemon:WarpUrl and AmlinLogging in ExpressManagerDaemon, HydraJobManagerDaemon, FileCopierDaemon and RatCatManagerDaemon.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Each daemon loads configuration through Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.
2. Daemon:WarpUrl and logging settings are available through JSON and environment variables.
3. Startup fails clearly when WarpUrl is required but absent.
4. Each daemon builds and starts using the new configuration path.

story: Move active runtime configuration to the .NET configuration model
title: Remove remaining active ConfigurationManager dependencies
implementationInstructions: Refactor active Factories and WorkflowManager.Domain paths that still obtain settings or connection strings through ConfigurationManager.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. No active source file calls ConfigurationManager for runtime settings.
2. Connection-string and application-setting dependencies are injected or supplied by typed options/factories.
3. Existing setting semantics are preserved.
4. The solution builds and representative runtime paths pass testing.

story: Move active runtime configuration to the .NET configuration model
title: Remove or exclude obsolete legacy configuration and generated artefacts
implementationInstructions: After active configuration reads have been migrated, review App.config files, transforms, generated Settings classes, installer/designer files and legacy AssemblyInfo files. Exclude or delete only after confirming they are not required by build or deployment tooling.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Each legacy artefact is classified as delete, exclude or retain temporarily.
2. Deleted files have no active references.
3. Project files no longer compile obsolete generated code.
4. The solution build and deployment packaging remain successful.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Move active composition to Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection
implementationInstructions: Replace host-level and worker-level ServiceBuilder calls with constructor injection and small factories for dependencies whose inputs are only known at runtime.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Active hosts compose services through IServiceCollection.
2. Workers do not call static ServiceBuilder methods.
3. Runtime-varying services use explicit factory interfaces.
4. The Factories project can be removed from consumers once no longer required.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Migrate ExpressManagerDaemon host composition to DI
implementationInstructions: Register the daemon, worker, API service, logging and related services in Program.cs and resolve the daemon from the service provider.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. ExpressManagerDaemon is created by DI rather than direct `new` or ServiceBuilder calls.
2. Constructor dependencies are explicit and null-checked.
3. Program.cs contains all host-level registrations.
4. The daemon starts and completes its existing smoke-test path.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Migrate HydraJobManagerDaemon host composition to DI
implementationInstructions: Replace direct ServiceBuilder construction in the Hydra job daemon host with IServiceCollection registrations and constructor injection.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The daemon is resolved from DI.
2. Host-level ServiceBuilder calls are removed.
3. Existing worker and API service lifetimes are preserved.
4. The daemon starts and the existing smoke-test scenario succeeds.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Migrate FileCopierDaemon host composition to DI
implementationInstructions: Register FileCopyWorker, WorkerService, WorkflowManagerApiService, logging and the daemon itself through Microsoft DI.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. FileCopierDaemon receives IWorkerService and logger through constructor injection.
2. FileCopierDaemon.csproj has no unnecessary Factories reference.
3. The solution builds.
4. A file-copy smoke test is completed when a representative workflow is available, or the limitation is documented.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Remove stale Factories project reference from FileCopierDaemon
implementationInstructions: Remove the FileCopierDaemon project reference to Factories after host-level ServiceBuilder usage has been eliminated and direct dependencies are declared.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. FileCopierDaemon.csproj no longer references Factories.csproj.
2. FileCopierDaemon source does not import MSAmlin.Express.Factories.
3. The daemon project and full solution build successfully.
4. DI registrations still resolve at startup.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Migrate RatCatManagerDaemon host composition to DI
implementationInstructions: Remove host-level ServiceBuilder use from RatCatManagerDaemon and resolve the daemon and its host dependencies through Microsoft DI.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The daemon host has no direct ServiceBuilder construction.
2. The solution builds successfully.
3. Runtime behaviour is preserved where it can be verified.
4. The lack of an active RatCat workflow is recorded as a release risk if testing cannot be completed.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Create task-message creator factory
implementationInstructions: Add ITaskMessageCreatorFactory in ServiceInterfaces and TaskMessageCreatorFactory in Services. Use the factory where task ID, task type and worker type are only known at execution time.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The interface exposes a Create method with task ID, task type and worker type.
2. The implementation returns the same concrete task-message creator previously produced by ServiceBuilder.
3. The factory is registered in each required host.
4. Worker code no longer calls ServiceBuilder for task-message creation.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Create file-copy service factory
implementationInstructions: Add IFileCopyServiceFactory in ServiceInterfaces and FileCopyServiceFactory in Services. Use it to create disposable file-copy service instances per operation.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The factory returns an IFileCopyService configured with the existing progress-reporting copier.
2. FileCopyWorker receives the factory through its constructor.
3. Each copy operation creates and disposes its own service instance.
4. FileCopyWorker contains no ServiceBuilder call.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Refactor Worker<T> and DatabaseWorker<T>
implementationInstructions: Inject task-message and database-service factories into the abstract worker hierarchy. Preserve task-specific server selection and message creation.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Worker<T> no longer imports MSAmlin.Express.Factories.
2. DatabaseWorker<T> obtains database services through an injected factory using task.ServerName.
3. Derived worker constructors are updated consistently.
4. Existing worker behaviour and error messages remain unchanged.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Refactor ExpressTaskRunner
implementationInstructions: Replace ServiceBuilder calls for express service, task-message creator and database service with injected factory abstractions.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. ExpressTaskRunner contains no ServiceBuilder calls.
2. Server-specific services are created using the task's server name.
3. Existing disposal and lifetime behaviour are preserved.
4. ExpressManagerDaemon smoke tests pass.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Refactor HydraJobWorker
implementationInstructions: Replace ServiceBuilder calls for WorkflowManager API services, Hydra job database services and general database services with injected services and factories.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. HydraJobWorker contains no ServiceBuilder calls.
2. Per-server Hydra job database services are created through a factory.
3. WorkflowManager API dependencies are injected with the correct worker identity and URL.
4. HydraJobManagerDaemon smoke tests pass.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Refactor RatCatWorker
implementationInstructions: Replace ServiceBuilder calls for RatCat database service, name validation and database attacher creation with explicit injected abstractions.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. RatCatWorker contains no ServiceBuilder calls.
2. Runtime-specific database attacher creation uses an explicit factory.
3. Existing validation and database attachment logic is unchanged.
4. The solution builds and the limited testability is recorded.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Remove Factories reference from Workers
implementationInstructions: Remove Workers.csproj's reference to Factories.csproj after all active ServiceBuilder and Factories namespace usage has been eliminated.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Workers.csproj no longer references Factories.csproj.
2. No source file in Workers imports MSAmlin.Express.Factories.
3. The project builds independently.
4. The complete solution and migrated daemon smoke tests pass.

story: Replace service location with explicit dependency injection
title: Refactor WorkflowManager.Domain ServiceBuilder usage
implementationInstructions: Treat WorkflowManager.Domain.ServiceBuilder as a separate cleanup stream. Replace active calls in ErrorService and task-success handlers with constructor injection or narrow factories.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Active domain services and handlers contain no static ServiceBuilder calls.
2. Sproto DAL and task-creator dependencies are explicit.
3. Commented-out legacy calls are removed or retained only with a justified note.
4. WorkflowManager.API.Core integration tests pass.

story: Preserve operational behaviour while modernising daemon hosts
title: Preserve daemon startup, shutdown and worker-thread behaviour
implementationInstructions: Ensure the .NET 10 daemons retain the operational semantics of the legacy service hosts, including startup logging, worker-thread creation, shutdown signalling, graceful join and exception handling.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Each daemon starts its worker path exactly once.
2. Shutdown signals are observed and worker threads terminate within the agreed timeout.
3. Startup, shutdown and unhandled exceptions are logged.
4. No daemon leaves foreground threads or undisposed services after shutdown.

story: Preserve operational behaviour while modernising daemon hosts
title: Validate daemon lifecycle and service-hosting assumptions
implementationInstructions: Review Program.cs and daemon classes for startup, cancellation, thread lifetime, disposal and deployment expectations. Confirm whether each daemon will run as a console process, scheduled process or managed Windows service.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Hosting mode is documented for each daemon.
2. Start and stop paths are testable without forcefully terminating the process.
3. Thread joins and timeouts are explicit.
4. Disposable services and service providers are disposed correctly.

story: Prove which legacy libraries affect the active solution
title: Classify legacy package usage within WARP_Prototype.Master.sln
implementationInstructions: Scan only projects currently included in WARP_Prototype.Master.sln and classify each legacy package as active runtime usage, reference-only, or absent.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The scan is generated from `dotnet sln ... list` rather than the whole repository.
2. Katana/OWIN, SignalR 2.2, Topshelf, EPPlus, ExcelLibrary, Castle Windsor and ServiceBuilder are covered.
3. Each result names the active project and file.
4. No conclusion relies on projects outside the active solution.

story: Prove which legacy libraries affect the active solution
title: Verify Katana and SignalR are absent from active projects
implementationInstructions: Search active solution projects for Microsoft.Owin, Owin, IAppBuilder, OwinStartup, SignalR packages, Hub types and SignalR client APIs.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Results are limited to active solution projects.
2. Any active code usage is listed separately from package-only references.
3. If no hits exist, the backlog records these as non-blocking for the active migration.
4. Build files are checked as well as source code.

story: Prove which legacy libraries affect the active solution
title: Verify Topshelf usage
implementationInstructions: Search active solution projects for Topshelf package references, HostFactory calls and Topshelf namespace imports.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. No active usage is assumed without a concrete file-level hit.
2. Any hit identifies whether it is package-only or executable code.
3. If no hits are found, no Topshelf replacement task is created.
4. The conclusion is documented in the migration scope.

story: Prove which legacy libraries affect the active solution
title: Verify EPPlus and ExcelLibrary usage
implementationInstructions: Search active solution projects for package references and concrete APIs such as OfficeOpenXml, ExcelPackage and ExcelLibrary workbook types.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Active code usage is distinguished from stale references.
2. Any required Excel export/import path is assigned a compatibility or replacement task.
3. Reference-only packages are removed from active project files.
4. Projects outside WARP_Prototype.Master.sln are ignored.

story: Prove which legacy libraries affect the active solution
title: Quantify Castle Windsor and ServiceBuilder coverage
implementationInstructions: Count active files and call sites that use Castle Windsor and ServiceBuilder. Report host-level, worker-level and domain-level coverage separately.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Castle Windsor results include package references, container creation, installers and registrations.
2. ServiceBuilder results include every active static call and Factories project reference.
3. Coverage is grouped by active project and runtime layer.
4. The DI migration backlog is updated only from confirmed active usage.

story: Prove that the migration retains existing business and integration behaviour
title: Define behaviour-preservation checks for migrated components
implementationInstructions: Create explicit compatibility checks for HTTP routes and verbs, DTO shapes, SQL/stored procedure calls, task messages, worker identity, progress events, configuration defaults, service lifetimes and disposal.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Each migrated component has a defined legacy-vs-.NET-10 comparison.
2. HTTP routes, verbs and payload shapes remain compatible where required.
3. Database calls and parameter mappings remain unchanged unless an approved change exists.
4. Worker messages, progress events and service lifetimes remain equivalent.

story: Prove that the migration retains existing business and integration behaviour
title: Create component-level compatibility checklists
implementationInstructions: For each migrated web endpoint, daemon and worker, document the observable legacy behaviour and the corresponding .NET 10 behaviour to be verified during testing.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Checklists exist for migrated endpoints, daemons and workers.
2. Each checklist includes inputs, outputs, side effects, logging and failure behaviour.
3. Any intentional difference is approved and linked to a decision.
4. The checklists are referenced by smoke, SIT and regression test tasks.

story: Remove legacy hosts after replacements are validated and behaviour-verified
title: Decommission legacy ExpressUI and WorkflowManager.API
implementationInstructions: After ExpressUI.Core and WorkflowManager.API.Core are functionally complete and their observable behaviour has been verified against the legacy hosts, remove the legacy host projects from WARP_Prototype.Master.sln. This is the solution-cleanup step deferred from the original STORY-001 so that the legacy hosts remain available as the discovery target and behaviour baseline until they are genuinely redundant. Source is retained on disk until release sign-off.
acceptanceCriteria: 1. Legacy ExpressUI and legacy WorkflowManager.API are absent from the active solution. 2. No active project retains a required reference to either legacy host. 3. All behaviour-preservation checks (STORY-014) for the replaced functionality are signed off before removal. 4. Legacy source remains on disk until release sign-off. 5. The solution builds successfully after removal.

story: Remove legacy hosts after replacements are validated and behaviour-verified
title: Remove legacy ExpressUI project from the active solution
implementationInstructions: Remove GUI\ExpressUI\UI.csproj from WARP_Prototype.Master.sln, leaving the source on disk for historical reference until release sign-off. Gated on ExpressUI.Core functional migration (STORY-007) being complete and its behaviour-preservation checks (STORY-014) signed off.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. UI.csproj no longer appears in `dotnet sln ... list`.
2. No active project retains a required project reference to UI.csproj.
3. The solution builds successfully after removal.
4. Any functionality still required from the old UI is represented by a separate backlog item.

story: Remove legacy hosts after replacements are validated and behaviour-verified
title: Remove legacy WorkflowManager API project from the active solution
implementationInstructions: Remove WorkflowManager\WorkflowManager.API\WorkflowManager.API.csproj from the solution and retain WorkflowManager.API.Core as the target API implementation. Leave the legacy source on disk until release sign-off. Gated on WorkflowManager API migration (STORY-008) being complete and behaviour-verified (STORY-014).
acceptanceCriteria:
1. The legacy WorkflowManager.API project is absent from the solution project list.
2. WorkflowManager.API.Core is the only active WorkflowManager API host.
3. No active project references the removed API project.
4. The solution builds successfully.

story: Validate the .NET 10 migration before production promotion
title: Complete technical and business validation
implementationInstructions: Verify compilation, startup, business workflows and non-functional requirements. Treat the migrated branch as a reference implementation until the required release testing is complete.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Clean restore and build succeed in the target build environment.
2. Required web/API and daemon smoke tests pass.
3. SIT and regression tests cover the agreed business scope.
4. Performance, security and operational checks are complete before production approval.

story: Validate the .NET 10 migration before production promotion
title: Run clean restore and full solution build
implementationInstructions: Delete or isolate generated output as appropriate, restore dependencies and build WARP_Prototype.Master.sln using the target .NET 10 SDK.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. `dotnet restore` completes successfully.
2. `dotnet build` completes with zero errors.
3. New warnings are reviewed and either resolved or accepted with justification.
4. The build uses only supported active projects.

story: Validate the .NET 10 migration before production promotion
title: Run ExpressUI.Core and WorkflowManager.API.Core smoke tests
implementationInstructions: Start both applications with representative configuration and exercise the migrated endpoints and primary DLM workflow.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Both applications start without unhandled exceptions.
2. Health/startup checks complete successfully.
3. Load import selection, load submission data and submit profiles endpoints return expected results.
4. Logs contain no new migration-related errors.

story: Validate the .NET 10 migration before production promotion
title: Run daemon smoke tests
implementationInstructions: Start and exercise ExpressManagerDaemon and HydraJobManagerDaemon. Test FileCopierDaemon and RatCatManagerDaemon when representative workflows and environments are available.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. ExpressManagerDaemon starts and processes a representative task.
2. HydraJobManagerDaemon starts and processes a representative task.
3. FileCopierDaemon and RatCatManagerDaemon are either tested successfully or recorded as explicit release risks.
4. Shutdown behaviour is clean and no worker threads are abandoned.

story: Validate the .NET 10 migration before production promotion
title: Complete SIT and regression testing
implementationInstructions: Execute the agreed business regression pack across UI, API, database and daemon workflows using representative environments and data.
acceptanceCriteria:
1. Test scope and entry/exit criteria are agreed.
2. All critical and high-priority scenarios pass.
3. Defects are triaged and blocking defects are resolved.
4. Business and technical owners approve the test outcome.
